coverage.note: A paper is rankable only when a cohort measuring its own field contains works from its own OpenAlex publication year. A cohort that begins after a paper's year cannot rank it at all, so the reason every unrankable paper is unrankable is published in unrankable_by_cause rather than left for a reader to infer from one coverage percentage.

fwci.explanation: Field-weighted citation impact: citations received in a work's first four years (its publication year plus the three that follow) divided by the citations expected for a work of that publication year, of that work type, in that OpenAlex subfield. 1.00 means a work attracted exactly what a comparable work would; 2.00 means twice as many. OpenAlex assigns the subfield from the work's own text rather than from its journal, splits articles into journal and conference proceedings, and applies no adjustment for an author's position on the paper. Age-matched and field-matched by construction, so it answers a comparison across publication years with no cohort download. Published by OpenAlex; nothing here computes it.

venues.explanation: The publication table prints each journal in the NLM (PubMed-compliant) abbreviation a reviewer recognises -- "J Med Chem", not "Journal of medicinal chemistry". That form is not derived by rule from the name; it is read from the "source" field of a PubMed esummary record, reached through a DOI published for a work in that journal, and cached in OpenAlex/journal-abbreviations.json. A venue the registry has no abbreviation for prints the name Google Scholar gave it, and a venue whose name does not match the registry's journal is never abbreviated.

programme_note: The anticoagulation and glycoscience papers are two literatures and are reported apart, at the user's instruction. Pooling them would hide the difference between the two mean FWCI figures, which is itself evidence about where the citation impact sits.
